title: Observability: metrics + traces for admission decisions, shed reasons, and breaker transitions
creator: Rafael Mendes
description:
Goal
Add end-to-end observability for overload protection so we can (a) distinguish intentional load shedding from internal failures, (b) debug why/where a request was shed, and (c) alert on breaker behavior (open/half-open flapping) and queue pressure before tail-latency collapses.

Scope
1) Metrics
- Admission control decisions at the edge/API gateway (allow/deny + reason + tier).
- Shed reasons across layers (gateway / routing / runtime), including bounded-queue sheds and memory-pressure/KV-cache guardrail sheds.
- Circuit breaker transitions and state (per (model, region, tier) key) including hysteresis/cooldown behavior.

2) Tracing
- Add trace/span attributes to propagate overload context from gateway → routing → runtime and back to client error response.
- Ensure OpenAI-compat endpoints keep consistent span naming/attributes.

3) Cardinality + standards
- Follow observability label/cardinality guidance (bounded sets; no raw customer IDs; route/model normalized).
- Sampling guidance for high-throughput paths.

Non-goals
- Building the dashboard/alert rules themselves (tracked in ENG-4830), though this ticket must expose the metrics required.
- Replacing existing quota/rate-limit metrics.

Proposed metric spec (draft)
Naming follows Redwood conventions: redwood.<component>.<signal>.<unit>

A) Edge / gateway
1. redwood.gateway.admission.decisions_total (counter)
- labels: decision={allow|deny}, reason_code, tier, region, endpoint_family={rest|openai_compat}, streaming={true|false}
- NOTE: no model label here unless already available and normalized (prefer routing layer for model granularity)

2. redwood.gateway.admission.latency_ms (histogram)
- labels: decision, tier, region, endpoint_family
- tracks time spent evaluating admission policy + breaker snapshot lookup (if applicable)

B) Routing / control plane
3. redwood.routing.breaker.state (gauge)
- labels: breaker_key_hash, region
- value mapping: 0=closed, 1=open, 2=half_open
- breaker_key_hash is a stable hash of (model, tier, capacity_pool, region) to keep labels bounded; raw labels emitted in logs/traces (sampled) only.

4. redwood.routing.breaker.transitions_total (counter)
- labels: from_state, to_state, trigger_signal, region
- trigger_signal examples: queue_depth, gpu_saturation, error_rate, latency_p99, manual_override

5. redwood.routing.breaker.open_duration_ms (histogram)
- labels: region, trigger_signal

6. redwood.routing.shed.decisions_total (counter)
- labels: layer=routing, reason_code, tier, region, model_family (bounded, e.g., llama, mistral, qwen)
- reason_code examples: BREAKER_OPEN, CAPACITY_UNAVAILABLE, FALLBACK_EXHAUSTED, POLICY_GUARDRAIL

C) Runtime / data plane
7. redwood.runtime.queue.depth (gauge)
- labels: pool, region, model_family

8. redwood.runtime.queue.shed_total (counter)
- labels: shed_point={enqueue|prefill_start|decode_start}, reason_code, pool, region, model_family
- reason_code examples: QUEUE_FULL, PREFILL_BACKPRESSURE, DECODE_STARVATION, KV_CACHE_PRESSURE, GPU_OOM_GUARD

9. redwood.runtime.scheduling.latency_ms (histogram)
- labels: phase={enqueue_to_prefill|prefill_to_decode|decode_step}, pool, region, model_family

D) Cross-cutting
10. redwood.overload.response_total (counter)
- emitted at gateway for responses that are overload-protected
- labels: http_status={429|503}, error_code (Redwood-specific), tier, region, endpoint_family

Tracing spec (draft)
- Ensure a single trace spans edge → routing → runtime.
- Add attributes (example names):
  - redwood.overload.decision={allow|deny}
  - redwood.overload.layer={gateway|routing|runtime}
  - redwood.overload.reason_code=<ENUM>
  - redwood.breaker.state={closed|open|half_open} (when evaluated)
  - redwood.breaker.key_hash=<stable hash>
  - redwood.request.tier={free|pro|enterprise}
  - redwood.request.streaming={true|false}
- Add an event on the active span when shedding occurs: event name="overload_shed" with reason_code + shed_point.
- Propagate reason_code and breaker snapshot via request context so downstream logs include it.

Cardinality constraints / notes
- DO NOT label metrics with: customer_id, org_id, raw model_name, raw route, prompt length buckets > small set.
- model_family must be from a small allowlist (maintained in routing config).
- breaker_key_hash required for breaker gauges to avoid exploding series.
- For debugging specific (model, region, tier), rely on (a) logs with sampling, (b) traces with sampling, (c) dashboards using filtered log queries.

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Gateway emits admission decision counter + latency histogram with correct labels, behind existing feature flag.
- [ ] Routing emits breaker state gauge + transitions counter + open duration histogram.
- [ ] Runtime emits queue depth gauge + shed counter with shed_point + reason_code.
- [ ] Gateway emits overload response counter aligned with ADR error taxonomy (429/503 + Redwood error code).
- [ ] Traces include overload attributes and an "overload_shed" event when applicable; propagation confirmed across gateway→routing→runtime.
- [ ] Metric label set reviewed for cardinality; series count estimate provided for us-east at peak.
- [ ] Example Grafana queries provided in ticket notes for ENG-4830.

Links / context

- Working notes: metric names + cardinality review: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/observability/metric-names-cardinality-review-overload.json

  - ENG-4822 (gateway admission control hook)
  - ENG-4824 (breaker state store/eval API)
  - ENG-4826 (runtime bounded queues + shed points)
  - ENG-4827 (runtime KV-cache/memory pressure guardrails)
- Dashboard/alerts ticket: ENG-4830

Implementation plan
1) Align on enums
- Finalize reason_code enums shared across layers (gateway/routing/runtime). Coordinate with Brian Murphy (API error semantics) to keep names consistent with customer-facing error codes.

2) Gateway instrumentation
- Implement counters/histograms in gateway middleware at decision point:
  - after classification (tier/streaming/endpoint_family)
  - before returning deny response
- Emit overload response_total at response writer after error mapping.

3) Routing instrumentation
- Instrument breaker evaluator:
  - on state transitions: transitions_total
  - on periodic state emission: state gauge (or export via in-memory collection)
  - on open durations: observe when closing from open → half-open/closed
- Add trace attributes when breaker evaluated.

4) Runtime instrumentation
- Emit shed_total at each shed point (enqueue/prefill/decode).
- Emit queue.depth gauge per pool.
- Add trace event on shed.

5) Sampling + perf
- Confirm hot path overhead (<1% p99 impact at canary load).
- Ensure metrics are aggregated; avoid per-request high-cardinality labels.

Open questions
- Do we need separate metrics for "shed due to breaker open" vs "shed due to queue full" at gateway if routing is unreachable? (proposal: yes, as reason_code differentiates.)
- Where to best emit breaker.state gauge: routing process metrics vs a small breaker-exporter? (proposal: routing emits; exporter optional later.)

- Validate no org_id/customer_id labels (spot-check Prometheus series + code review).

Notes for ENG-4830 (example queries)
- Shed rate by reason: sum(rate(redwood_runtime_queue_shed_total[5m])) by (reason_code, shed_point, region)
- Breaker transition spikes: sum(rate(redwood_routing_breaker_transitions_total[5m])) by (to_state, trigger_signal, region)
- Overload response mix: sum(rate(redwood_overload_response_total[5m])) by (http_status, error_code, region, tier)
